verdicts.reasoning: Verified both sides exist exactly as quoted. Step 8's contract, reinforced again at the convergence re-run (line 889), is unambiguously test-first TDD: write failing tests, then implement to green. flutter-expert's own Core Workflow orders State (2) -> Widgets (3, build components, run tests after each feature) -> Test (4, write widget/integration tests) -- i.e. code-then-test, the opposite order. flutter-expert is one of the named lane skills a track subagent loads directly alongside sprint-execution/test-driven-development at step 8 (KICKOFF.md line 607), so an implementer literally following the skill's own numbered workflow would build widgets before writing their tests, violating the step's TDD requirement. This is a genuine behavioral disagreement (contradiction), not incidental phrasing overlap, and not a load-bearing parameter since neither side is supplying a parameter to the other -- they simply prescribe conflicting orderings. Severity stays low: the KICKOFF block that names flutter-expert (line 607) doesn't itself restate an ordering, so the clash is between the step's general contract and the skill's internal steps rather than a direct per-invocation instruction; also flutter-expert's numbered list plausibly reads as a default standalone workflow rather than a hard sequencing rule that overrides an explicitly invoked TDD skill. Same underlying tension is systemic across other lane skills (e.g. kotlin-specialist), which the queue entry already notes via raised_by/other_locations.
